titulo: Stock Buybacks and Layoffs: Cognex, $2.32M Per Cut
caption:
Stock Buybacks and Layoffs: Cognex, $2.32M Per Cut

Stock buybacks and layoffs, same company, same year: Cognex.
From the archive: May 2020. Not today's news.
Cognex, May 26, 2020 (Cognex, Form 8-K (Item 2.05)): "reduce the Company’s operating costs, optimize its business model"
Cognex's May 2020 8-K approved a restructuring plan with a reduction in force of approximately 190 employees. Its 2020 10-K reports $441.5 million in cash paid for repurchases and dividends.

That same year: $441.5 million to shareholders, 2020, company-wide. $51.036 million of repurchases (a buyback is when a company buys its own shares back from the market) plus $390.508 million of dividends in 2020, company-wide (cash flow statement, in thousands). The dividend line includes a one-time special dividend paid in the fourth quarter.
The math: $441.5 million to shareholders, 2020, company-wide ÷ about 190 jobs = $2.32 million to shareholders in 2020 per job cut. The result is approximate. A ratio, not a cause.
The facts: $441.5 million to shareholders, 2020, company-wide (Cognex 10-K, FY2020, Feb 11, 2021). About 190 planned job cuts (Cognex 8-K, May 2020, May 28, 2020). The 190 cuts come from the May 2020 8-K; the payouts come from the 2020 10-K.

An 8-K is the report a US public company files with the SEC when something material happens. A 10-K is its annual report.

Do companies do buybacks and layoffs in the same year? Here is one that did, on paper, from two SEC filings.

Optimize the shareholder column. (Our take.)

Send this to someone who has been through a round of cuts.
